title: Memory Management Is the New Code
one_liner: Treat shared memory as the maintained interface between human intent and model action.
problem: Persisting agent memory is no longer the difficult part. A folder in a Git repository already provides a strong default: it is versioned, diffable, reviewable and portable. The harder problems appear after memories accumulate. A human may not be able to see what the agent currently believes; an initially clear structure may decay as entries and links multiply; and obsolete guidance may remain plausible enough to be recalled. These failures are operational, not merely archival: an invisible or stale belief can steer the next action.
solution: Keep durable shared memory as small, addressable files in a dedicated, version-controlled folder, with an index that supports deliberate recall. Store one durable assertion per file, link related assertions, and record corrections as explicit successors rather than silently rewriting history. Make every recall inspectable by showing the files, excerpts and revision used. Review the index and staleness signals as maintained interfaces. Use another store only when a narrow requirement—ephemeral state, high-volume events, cross-repository retrieval at scale, or access controls that Git cannot provide—justifies the extra synchronization path.
